newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus c.bank chief says seeks convertibility.
newsitem.headline: Belarus c.bank chief says seeks convertibility.

text.p: Central Bank chief Gennady Alexinikov said on Thursday that Belarus was aiming for full convertibility of its rouble currency.

"Of course the final aim of re-forming the currency market is to adhere to the International Monetary Fund's Article Eight, and achieve full convertibility of the Belarussian rouble," Aleinikov said in an address at a ceremony marking the 75th anniversary of the banking system.
He was speaking after the publication in an official newspaper of a decision saying a market rouble/dollar rate policy had been introduced.
The National Bank will now set a daily rate based on supply and demand at the Minsk Interbank Currency Exchange, adjusted for inflation, it said.
He predicted that full currency reforms would not be implemented "before April at the earliest".
International lending bodies have stopped lending money to Belarus pending faster reforms, and one of their biggest concerns is exchange rate policy.
In February the Belarus government introduced a fixed rate of 22,050 Belarussian roubles per dollar.
President Alexander Lukashenko keeps a tight grip on banks and prices. Economic reforms are ruinning at a much slower pace than in many other former Soviet republics.
